frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #11: 'Add restart-safe migration scaffolding for legacy plaintext values: read legacy, validate, write encrypted, read back/verify, then erase plaintext. No automatic migration executes until S6 authorization/physical-presence policy exists.' -- implemented exactly this six-step sequence (check destination first for restart-safety, then read/validate/write/read-back-verify/erase), entirely on top of the existing Section 2.7-2.9 primitives; nothing in this repository calls secure_storage_migrate_str(), matching the plan's own 'no automatic migration executes' text literally.

S5's 'Error, transaction and concurrency behavior' contract text: 'Interrupted encrypted migration remains restart-safe and never deletes plaintext before encrypted readback succeeds.' -- directly implemented via the destination-first restart-safety check and the strict ordering (erase only ever happens after a successful readback-verify, whether that verify happened this call or a previous one).

This project's established real-tool-grounding discipline was applied to the new nvs_erase_key() call exactly as it was to esp_flash_encryption_enabled() in the prior sub-slice: the real signature and documented return codes (including ESP_ERR_NVS_NOT_FOUND for an already-erased/never-written key) were confirmed via grep inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before writing any code referencing it.

erase_primitive_implemented.detail: hal_nvs_erase_key() follows hal_nvs.c's exact existing per-function pattern (nvs_open/operation/nvs_commit/nvs_close on ESP_PLATFORM). Confirmed the real nvs_erase_key(nvs_handle_t, const char*) signature and its ESP_ERR_NVS_NOT_FOUND-for-nonexistent-key behavior via a real grep inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before implementing. Host mock is type-agnostic: searches all three internal per-type tables (u32/str/blob) since a real NVS key carries no type tag at this API level, and clears whichever table actually holds it. secure_storage_erase() layers the same namespace-ownership gate as the read/write paths on top, and treats NOT_FOUND as success (kErased) -- deliberately idempotent, since a caller retrying an interrupted cleanup step must not have to distinguish 'already gone' from 'just removed'.

migration_scaffolding_implemented.detail: secure_storage_migrate_str() implements the plan's own six-step sequence entirely through Sections 2.7-2.9's existing primitives (secure_storage_get_str/set_str/erase), so their namespace-ownership, fail-closed-encryption-gate and idempotent-erase guarantees apply automatically. Destination is checked first (restart-safety: an existing valid destination value means a prior call already migrated, so no re-read/re-validate/re-write happens, only a best-effort source cleanup retry). Source read failure states (not-provisioned, corrupt, unavailable) each get a distinct result value. A caller-supplied validator gates migration on content. The destination write goes through the plan #12 encryption-verified gate automatically. Readback verification happens strictly before any erase attempt.

design_flaw_found_and_fixed_during_this_.status: COMPLETE -- caught by writing this sub-slice's own tests, not a separate review
design_flaw_found_and_fixed_during_this_.detail: An initial draft allowed source and destination to name the literal same namespace+key (reasoning this project's transparent whole-partition NVS Encryption might make an in-place rewrite a valid real migration path). Attempting to write a test for that case surfaced that the destination-first restart-safety check cannot distinguish 'already migrated' from 'legacy value simply present, never migrated' when source and destination are the same slot -- meaning the plan #12 encryption-verified write gate would be silently, permanently bypassed for any pre-existing value. Fixed by adding an explicit upfront rejection (SecureStorageMigrationResult::kInvalidSameSourceAndDestination) before secure_storage_migrate_str() touches storage at all, and documenting the reasoning directly in the header. Verified via a dedicated test (test_same_source_and_destination_rejected_outright).
